utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Mr. Karadzic, you will have for your cross-examination the same amount of time as what Prosecution had for its examination-in-chief, which means you will have two hours and 20 minutes for today, since you had spent two hours and half yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Does this proviso state that if things run smoothly there'll be extra time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, please continue cross-examination and --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Excellency, good morning. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Is there a way of somehow obtaining the video-tape that you mentioned showing the Patriotic League Assembly in Godus, and if so, in what way can we do that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may provide it either to you or the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would be very grateful to you. Can you tell us the name of the Muslim author of the book which describes the preparations for the war by the Muslims in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The book is entitled the -- Zvornik from the elections --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the witness please repeat clearly the name of the book.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you repeat the name of the book.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The title is "Zvornik From the Elections to the Dayton Agreement."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we now have in e-court 1D3938. Yesterday, we discussed the subject relating to the volunteers who came and were accepted and equalised with every other military conscript. I'm going to ask you now whether that was a customary -- I'm afraid this is not the right document. It's 1D3938. We're surely going to need this document, but only later because this is a significant Muslim document. Can we then put the document on the ELMO if it is not uploaded in the e-court, but it should have been. Oh, I apologise. It's 3998. I made a mistake. Is this a list of the volunteers in voluntary detachment in the Drina Corps, which show that maximum 10 or 12 of them were assigned to each unit and that care was taken for ensuring their status, and the army did not allow the volunteers to be concentrated in one unit but, rather, distributed them all over their strength?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before that, Mr. Witness, could you tell us what this document is about?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document -- actually, a list of volunteers assigned to units of the Army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Who wrote it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Drina Corps, but I don't see any signature.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. How do you know that this is written --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Although I see it for the first time, I can read in the title that it says the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Among other things, was this done because of the bad experience that they had with larger units that prompted the Army of Republika Srpska not to allow the volunteers to be in larger units but just merge them in their own units?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. From the very day when the Army of Republika Srpska was established, they took good care of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I can't read it. Does it have a date? Do we know when this is from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I'm not satisfied, speaking for myself, as to its provenance and the date as well. I don't think the witness is in the position to tell us about it. Who wrote it and when was it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I see it for the first time and I can only read what it says. Otherwise I have no detailed knowledge about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I don't think this witness is able to give any provenance about this document, and I -- I don't think it is appropriate to admit this document through this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There was something that remained unclear to me. Is it true that -- that Rade Kostic worked at the MUP of Croatia? Is it possible that he lost his job there, that he was registered in Serbia, but that, nevertheless, he remained in Serbian Krajina where he had worked before?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He worked at the Croatian MUP, and he was a police station commander when Croatia was in existence. When the war broke out, he joined the Republic of Serbian Krajina and discharged the duties of the assistant minister for the interior. The minister was Mr. Martic, but I don't know in which period that took place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, he was not an employee of the MUP of Serbia; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The other day I saw for the first time a document indicating that he was in the MUP of Serbia, but at the time, he wasn't. He was in the Republic Serbian of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that Mr. Radmilo Bogdanovic, the then -- or the former minister of the interior was at the time in charge of the Serbs living outside of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said. He was chairman of the Assembly committee providing for the Serbs outside of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did he instruct you to make also links with the TO to co-operate with the JNA and to co-operate with the Republic of Serbian Krajina with regard to the procurement of weapons, and did he accept your assessment of the threat posed by the arming of the Muslims?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we did our best to provide as many arguments in that respect as possible, and I think that we provided convincing arguments to the effect that the Muslims were indeed arming themselves, so he instructed us to work closely with the army, and he also referred us to Kostic in the Serbian Republic of Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that any relevant person not taking into account anonymous telephone calls like the one we read yesterday, so did any relevant personality inform the party HQ about the procurement of weapons and other developments?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Nobody did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Excuse me, I just wonder what call Mr. Karadzic is referring to if he can talk about yesterday. The intercept he showed us was not anonymous. It had the name of each of the caller.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, but the witness says that such a person did not exist in Zvornik. Somebody was probably giving a false name. At least such a person did not exist within the authority structures in Zvornik. That's what the witness says.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Zvornik is a small town. We basically knew everybody else, and I'm not familiar with the person of that name ever existing in Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's wrap up the subject of Arkan. Is it true that Arkan came to Zvornik twice and stayed for a day or for an hour on each occasion; is that right? I think I saw it somewhere in the documents?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that he came twice and that he stayed for an hour on each occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. His representative was Major Pejic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And he stayed in Zvornik for about seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Arkan came to Zvornik as a hero, that he had been highly commended in Bijeljina, that the Muslims invited him to their homes and were grateful to him because he resolved that crisis in a matter of 24 hours?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that he came to Bijeljina as a hero, and I know that while he was passing through these places some celebrations were organised. He came to Zvornik as a hero, too, exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: However, the Muslim paper "Oslobodjenje" didn't write about him in complementary terms.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I was able to read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you were not always able to distinguish who the people were who appeared and offered assistance? Only after you talked between Marko Pavlovic and General Jankovic, you found out that he was an influential person?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since we were, as I said, a state within a state and none of us had any significant military experience in such situations, the Crisis Staff behaved as a sort of naive flock of sheep. Whoever who came and offered anything, we welcomed that. Therefore, there were some contradictory decision taken. There were some unreasonable moves made, and I think that some of the decisions led to a complete chaos. The people who came from outside even exacerbated this chaotic situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that Vojislav Jekic mentioned here by another witness also represented himself and pretended to be more important than he was and that you were not aware of his exact position in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that the same situation with Zuca, Pivarski, Niski, and all the rest of them who came there just to impress the authorities until they gained power?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the situation at the beginning. Niski, for example, would go to beat up a whole unit, to force them to take their clothes off and walk through villages, and several units experienced this, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you referring to the Serbian TO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. When they became a very strong group, they were really rampaging around and doing what they wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know that Arkan was not closely related to the MUP of Serbia but, rather, the federal MUP while the minister was Slovenian Stane Dolanc, and is it true that he used to come to Zvornik with a car bearing the licence plate with the number 900 which indicates the federal MUP property?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that he came in an official car that had 900 licence plates, whereas all other republics had their own numbers. Nine hundred indicated the federal SUP, which created a terrible confusion among us. Seeing him coming in this official car with official licence plates, and he was just passing by all the policemen on the ground in that car.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Were you aware that there was an antagonism between the federal MUP and the MUP of Serbia which eventually resulted in the takeover of facilities and nearly an armed conflict between the two?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were the rumours and were they founded that some private institutes from Belgrade were the rightful owners of Glinica which exported goods daily, the value amounting to a million dollars and some groups were paid by those owners to protect their investments?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. And there were some groups that came to the staff and were unwilling to join any TO units. They were saying that they had been tasked with guarding that property that belonged to the institute of physical chemistry in Belgrade and possibly some other private companies, and they deployed around Glinica and that's where they stayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us now focus on Kozluk. Is it correct to say that the position of Kozluk can be divided into three stages: The first one being from the elections till the outbreak of the conflict; the second from that point till the end of the regular functioning of the authorities; and the third stage beginning with the moment when the paramilitaries suspended the regular military authorities?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could one say that the Muslim population at Kozluk mostly voted for the SDA, and the Serbian population for the SDS, as in of all of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could one say that there were no problems in Kozluk during that first stage from the elections until April 1992, that life was mostly normal?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was life normal in spite of the fact that there were volunteers from Kozluk and Zvornik in Croatia who fought with the Croatian MUP against the Serbs in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that at the beginning of the conflict a considerable number of Muslim youths from Kozluk went to Muslim-controlled territory, that's the territory of today's federation, to fight with the Patriotic League or the BH Army?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the neighbouring village, Sepak, have a unit of the Patriotic League? Is Sepak the neighbouring village?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Sepak is some 7, 8 kilometres away from Kozluk, but like all Muslim populated villages, they had a local unit of the Patriotic League.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in spite of that, life was normal in Kozluk and that there were normal relations between Kozluk and the Serbs all this time?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, once conflicts broke out in Zvornik itself, and they lasted for two or three days, is it correct that after that at some point in time the Muslims from Kozluk got ready, packed their things, and demanded to be transported or allowed to go to the territory around Kalesija and Tuzla, which is the territory that today belongs to the federation?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that. Is it correct that the authorities, even Arkan and Pejic, were against their departure and that a large meeting was called, a meeting of the most renowned Muslims and Serbs, attended by --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat these names he's now reading out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The municipal authorities, Serbian municipal authorities from Zvornik and even Arkan's Major Pejic, and that they were able to dissuade the Muslims from leaving, and that the Muslims got everything they had demanded as was said before court in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The Muslims at Kozluk and Sepak and the surrounding villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you note the line 17, 18 by transcript page, by interpreter's note. They couldn't follow the names you read out and missed that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The highest ranking representative of the Serbian Orthodox Church, Bishop Vasilije, who had arrived from Bijeljina. He used to live in Bijeljina, but he fled and went to Bijeljina [as interpreted]. And from the Serbian side, there were also the municipal authorities, the authorities of the Serbian municipality of Kozluk. And the Muslims side was represented by Mufti Lugavic from Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that his real name is Lugonjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Possible. Lugonjic from Tuzla. Then Dr. Muhamed Jelkic, who was a member of both the Serbian and the Muslim Crisis Staff that we spoke about already, and then there was Arkan's Major Pejic. And at that meeting guarantees were given and the Muslims were persuaded to stay; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Bishop Vasilije. His bishopric was called the Zvornik-Tuzla bishopric, with its seat in Tuzla. But he fled and went to Bijeljina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In line 7, or 6 and 7, I seem not to have been sufficiently clear. Tuzla was not recorded again. So he fled from Tuzla and went to Bijeljina, and he came to this meeting from Bijeljina which was some 50 kilometres away to persuade the Muslims to stay; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us what the Muslims then got for not leaving?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please don't mention that.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No problem? Okay.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then we agreed that for reasons of security and safety joint patrols should be organised with an equal representation of Serbs and Muslims and who should keep law and order at Kozluk and that supplies should be improved, especially food supplies, because there were shortages of food already, and then that there should be an outpatient clinic. And then we also discussed other forms of co-operation in accordance with their needs, and while I was a member of the Crisis Staff I know that all -- that this agreement was implemented perfectly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that after that, Grujic personally drove sick women and children to Loznica to be treated, and did I understand correctly that a new police station was set up there with both Muslim and Serbian personnel? Was that -- was it that way?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the meeting I remember that Grujic took some people who were in need of medical treatment to Loznica, to the local hospital. And a new station was set up with the proportional representation of Serbs and Muslims for both groups to be safe, and all that functioned without a single incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thanks. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I see the word (redacted) but the witness didn't say that. Okay. It's all right now. Were the relations with the Muslim leaders from Kozluk, such as Fadil Banjanovic and others, fair and regular during those three months?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the separation line 2 or 3 kilometres away from Kozluk, the front line, that is, and were the people in Kozluk and Sepak able to hear the shooting from the separation line? And Vitnica was about 5 or -- 5 kilometres away, but the separation line was closer, and Vitnica was a Muslim stronghold even today and the -- in the federation of BiH.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Apart from the fact that the front line was so close, and although wounded people returned from the front line and some people got killed and soldiers went there -- went there to rotate shifts, in a word the situation was not pleasant at all, was there still a feeling of safety while the municipal authorities were functional during those three months while that -- while those people were still in Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that through Kozluk and -- through Kozluk a large number of refugees, Serbian refugees, came to Zvornik, who fought -- had fought their way out of Muslim-controlled territory, Zivinice, Tuzla, Kalesija and that they passed through Kozluk, and that in Zvornik their there were about 15- to 20.000 of them?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did that contribute to the rise of tensions, and is it a fact that while the municipal authorities were functional, in spite of that they did not ask to be left -- to leave Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you now about similar Serbian inhabited places in the Muslim-controlled territory.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the -- his last sentence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is Dubnica -- there seem to be problems with our toponyms. Is Dubnica a similar Serbian settlement in the Kalesija municipality, which is between Zvornik and Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber or -- excuse me. Were there similar concentrations in the periphery of Tuzla, Simin Han and Zanice [as interpreted]? Are those Serbian settlements?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is Rastosnica a large concentration of Serbian hamlets amounting to 2500 or even 4.000 inhabitants to the north-west of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please tell the Trial Chamber what happened to these Serbian settlements that are comparable to Kozluk, and let us explain immediately that this is not tu quoque. We merely want to explain how refugees came to Zvornik and what their state -- their prevailing state of mind was. What happened to Serbian settlements in the Muslim-controlled territory?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were attacked by Muslim armed forces. Some inhabitants were killed and others fled to Serbian-controlled territory. Most of them to Zvornik, especially all of Rastosnica and a large part of Dubnica, actually, all of Dubnica and a smaller part of Simin Han and the other where the church is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Pozarnica.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Pozarnica. Pozarnica and Simin Han mostly left in the direction of Bijeljina, whereas Rastosnica and Dubnica [Realtime transcript read in error "Dubrovnik"] in the direction of Zvornik, and their churches were destroyed there and their houses burned, and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps I can help the court reporter. It's Dubnica. It's not Dubrovnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But Simin Han and Pozarnica are the other two places; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The other locality is Rastosnica with many Serbian hamlets, Rastosnica; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us shed some light on the third stage, the final stage in the fate of Kozluk. Power in Zvornik had been taken over by paramilitaries; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: (redacted) (redacted) You confirmed that the Muslims in Kozluk at that moment were in real danger, and that after the three months while the authorities were functional once the authorities were suspended they found themselves in real danger; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did they know that the paramilitaries --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I apologise for interrupting. Can we -- private session for one moment?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Did I understand correctly that if I only say 1D and then the number of document and the number of page we needn't go into private session? Is that what Mr. Nicholls understood?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that's fair enough.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So did the Muslims of Kozluk know about the paramilitary units maltreating members of the authorities that were taking them out to be shot? They were beating them and humiliating them.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, was it possible for the Muslims to expect from such badly treated and humiliated authorities to receive any protection during the three months?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was there any plan to have the Serbian areas cleansed from Muslims? Would the Muslims of Kozluk be retained or would they be allowed to leave the territory immediately?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They would have been allowed to leave the territory immediately. However, there was no such plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can one conclude with certainty that nobody in the authority structures or in political parties -- was there at least any wish for the Muslims to leave? On the contrary, they thought it was desirable for Muslims to stay behind?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Even nowadays is Kozluk still in Republika Srpska and the municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we say that both in Kozluk and in Divic the huge majority, if not all of them, returned, and I'm talking about those people who were refugees at the time?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you remember, was there ever denial of the right of the refugees to come back, and was our position always clear to the effect that everything related to refugees was of a temporary nature, their status and their property?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let me remind you now of yesterday's page 19 in the transcript when my learned friend Mr. Nicholls presented to you a portion of Mladic's notebook. Do you remember that at this meeting Branko Grujic said, We were the most productive in evacuating the Muslims? This is what was read from that notebook.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was what was read, but I was not at that meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us establish this: A similar sentence was uttered --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just -- this may be of assistance. I think Mr. Karadzic was referring to what Marko Pavlovic said at the meeting. It was Pavlovic who said, We were most active in evicting Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that that was said by Mr. Grujic, and I would like, if possible, to have this document so that we can check it out in e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you upload it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we are waiting, I'm going to now tell you a similar situation. Dr. Novakovic said a similar sentence in Bijeljina relating to a certain person, that he was doing this thing best, and later on he and another group of MPs filed a criminal report. Is it characteristic of our mentality to use irony or sarcasm when we say he's doing nothing apart from what he's not supposed to do? Do you agree, and do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am familiar with this first portion that refers to Bijeljina. Everybody in the republic knows that Novakovic and another group of SDS MPs filed a criminal report against the man who was involved in the evictions of Muslims. I agree with you that it is consistent with our mentality to boast about things that they didn't do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At this meeting, whether there was lunch involved or not, was Mr. Grujic allowed to raise any objections against Captain Dragan and other things since Mr. Mladic and I --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please pause between questions and answers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Interpreters find it very difficult to follow you when you overlap in such a degree. Yes, Mr. Nicholls. Could you identify the page number of that Exhibit 1478?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: It should be 252 and 253 in the English, Your Honours. And I believe 249 and 2 --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps even 244, if I remember correctly from yesterday. Let's try 244, where Grujic is speaking. The next one, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's page 249 where Branko Grujic started speaking, starting saying, "We have 32.000 Serbs." 249.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the Serbian version as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 249. This is 252. The e-court page 249. Yes, but e-court page 249. Is it correct? Branko Grujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. I believe -- well, it actually may be 247 in the B/C/S, 249 in the English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next page for English now. Yes. We have the identical pages for both languages.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Here Mr. Grujic says, "We have 32.000 Serbs," and he says: "We have successfully implemented the president's decision to settle Divic and Kozluk with our children." Do you remember that from the highest level an order was publicised for the abandoned property to be considered as temporary, that refugees and such occurrences are normal in a war and that those properties cannot be given for use to the local residents?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will now provide a reference for all the parties involved and tell -- I'm going to tell you where you confirmed, and that was 1D3987, page 49. You confirmed there that no changes occurred in ownership over immovable property in the municipality throughout the war.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The ownership relations remained unchanged, and I know the local authorities issued temporary decisions allocating the abandoned property to the Serbs who had fled from the federation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They had the duty of care, and they were obliged to return it once the time come for that. Did they return the property to the Muslim of Kozlic and Divic -- Kozluk and Divic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the decision, and these properties were returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Has it been resolved who it was who said that they were productive in evacuating Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I don't believe so, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I think that we cannot talk about expulsion and evacuation, rather, but if we look at the next page, maybe we can find this, and that is actually a continuation of Grujic's speech. I believe that we need the next pages in both versions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here that we didn't have enough officers, and after that, Pavlovic is speaking about the problems with paramilitary. He mentioned Glinica by saying that there were armed men in Glinica.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All of this is being spoken about by Grujic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Oh, that's right. So he said there were no other officers except this Pavlovic person. He's also mentioning Glinica, and he says that, We had to get rid of Zuca and Captain Dragan, which was his wish.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And he says that they burst into the municipal building again that morning and took them prisoner.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He speaks here about all the industrial facilities grinding to a halt. So I cannot find this in this portion, so I'll have to look at yesterday's transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If we scroll through the next two pages, we'll see the reference I believe he was referring to.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. That would be fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Bottom of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So he's telling everybody what is not operational in Zvornik. He's also talking about conflicts between the brigades and armed civilians, and it says: "We were most active in evicting the Muslims." So all of this is being spoke be by Grujic; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. These are the words uttered by Pavlovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we go back so that we can see exactly the beginning of Pavlovic's contribution?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 251, e-court page 251 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah-ha. This is correct. Number 5, this is where it begins. My mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Nicholls. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Never mind. So this Pavlovic, who at the time was commander of the TO, did he talk about the things that were not being done in Zvornik, and he is being sarcastic about what is being done, and is it true that the Muslims were not removed while the municipal authorities were operational, and Pavlovic was part of that authority?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But once the paramilitary were put to prison, Pavlovic was also imprisoned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yesterday and today there have been a series of huge compound questions being read out to the witness to which the answer is usually one word. I have not objected up to this point. For this question, I do object to that much being packaged into one question, and I do wonder how the witness is supposed to know what was being in the mind of Marko Pavlovic when he spoke and whether he was being sarcastic at a meeting he was not present at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Fair enough. I agree with you. Bear that in mind, Mr. Karadzic, when putting the questions. Yes, you like to comment on it? Yes, Mr. Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I started my answer by saying, "Yes," but when these paramilitary units were imprisoned, he was imprisoned with them, and we were all surprised at that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I acknowledge the objection raised by Mr. Nicholls but this is due to my haste because of shortage of time. Let us clarify this. At the time was Marko Pavlovic participating in the authorities that were under the pressure of the paramilitary units? Was he in favour or against emigration?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he was participating in the authorities that were under the pressure of paramilitary. Now, speaking about emigration, I don't know who was in favour of what. All I know, that once two sides engage in war, civilians tend naturally to run towards their respective armies. If we are talking about Kozluk, quite simply nobody was able to prevent them. They wanted to join their own ethnic community, and they wanted to flee. I know that although we reached an agreement, several hundreds of them moved through the forests and joined the army. We had a list of how many of them were in April 1992 and how many of them left. While they were moving out in June or July, there were 1.600 of them only. Where are the remaining 1.200, because Kozluk had between 3- and 4.000 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now I would like us to deal with a different topic. What is repeated often in the indictment is that the Serbs took over many municipalities, so I would like to ask you to help us shed more light on that particular matter. Is it correct, actually, that the elections in 1990 were a kind of substitute for the census and that the Serbs prevailingly voted for the SDS, the Croats for the HDZ, and the Muslims for the SDA?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Serbs won absolute power in 37 out of 109 municipalities and that in another 10 municipalities they won power relatively and that in the republican government they had more than one-third?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we take into account the fact that in four or five Croatian municipalities in Western Herzegovina there was never any Serb population, hence they could not one the elections either, does that mean that in 47 municipalities the Serb Democratic Party on behalf of the Serb people had a majority government, and in the remaining municipalities they had a considerable participation in government?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: One of these 57 municipalities where we did not have absolute power but we had a significant participation or share in government was the municipality of Zvornik; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that in Bijeljina we had absolute government or authority insistently from the elections from 1990 until the present day?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that in Bijeljina we were in power on the 30th and 31st of March in 1992, and on the 1st, 2nd, 3rd, and any other April from 1992 to the present day?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that with the exception of Bijeljina and Sekovici where they were a prevalent majority, the Serbs controlled, at least until mid-1993, only their own parts of the remaining municipalities, whereas Muslim territory was controlled by Muslim forces?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask -- just a moment, please. I kindly ask for your understanding.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D14141, please. 14141 is the 65 ter number. It's not in colour, actually, but could we please zoom in a bit more. Could the usher please help the witness by giving him an electronic pen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please, could you put a circle around the town of Zvornik itself and place number 1 there.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you now circle Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And could you put number 2 there.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that these light areas are parts of the municipality where the Serbs constitute an absolute majority, Jadran, Jovici, Karakaj, Grbavci, Kruglic? Do you see all of these locations?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are all of these Serb areas?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who controlled these villages during the first year of the war? Can you mark the front line for us there approximately?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Towards the end of 1992, roughly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did we control Godus?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we did not. However, I have difficulty finding my way here. How can I mark this approximately? Approximately, I tried to do this very quickly, but I think it is about 90 per cent correct. We only controlled this area facing the Drina, the white area and this area here towards the Drina. And we had access to Sekovici. That is this road here from Karakaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To Caparde?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to Caparde. And that is how we controlled it. Actually, in 1993, more of the municipality was controlled by the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put a circle around Kozluk and place number 3 there.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see Vitnica? It was a Muslim settlement, and it remained under their control.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is Vitnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. These villages, Savici [phoen], Zavrsje, and so on, these other Serb villages --

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Zavrsje, Sajicic [phoen], Cevir [phoen], all of that was taken by the Muslim army in 1992, and they linked up with Teocak from here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Lazle [phoen], all of that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these are Serb villages that the Muslims took in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you kindly put number 4 for Vitnica for future reference.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm afraid that we've crippled the transcript. So the Serb villages to the west of Vitnica, that is to say to the west of the separation line, immediately fell under the control of the Muslims; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What happened to these villages and this population?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some of them fell victim and those who did not fall victim fled to Zvornik and had the status of refugees.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How many of them stayed to the west of Vitnica -- or, rather, to the west of the separation line?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This has to do with a relocation of, say, 5- to 6.000 inhabitants.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And no Serbs stayed there during the war?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I think that to this day it is possible that not more than 100 people live to the west of Vitnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you explain this to the Trial Chamber: To the south of Zvornik, Snagovo, Milosevici and these other villages, is it correct that all the way to up to Cerska which is near Vlasenica but which is close to the border, were they under the control of the Muslim forces for an entire year?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All of them except for this very small part of Drinjaca and this area along the Drina. Now, what was the name of this other Serb village there? That was not under their control. All the rest was controlled by the Muslims, all of it. So we did not actually have access to Pale and Sarajevo via Ceparde and Sekovici only, and that was partly taken and people were killed there in passing, on trucks, and it was very unsafe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we put number 5 by Drinjaca, and number 6 should mark the road that they controlled for all of one year towards Pale and Milici, from Zvornik towards Milici, Vlasenica and Pale, that is.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot see that very well. I cannot see where Drinjaca is, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Drinjaca, it says A. You see, Belonasilje [phoen]. It's a Serb settlement because it's white. Luzani.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Luzani.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No, the part that you marked.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, by the crossroads, right. That's number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 5, Drinjaca. You can put number 5 next to the circle.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, do we see that road that was under their control for a year?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, here it is. That is the road that links Zvornik with Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And Drinjaca between 5 and 1, was that also controlled by them for a year?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. All the way up to Divic. Their [as interpreted] defence line was by the Vidikovac Hotel at Divic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please put a circle around Divic and place number 6 next to it. You don't have to put it inside. You can put it next to it.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Our defence line was "there," not "theirs," as the transcript says.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's where the separation line was. We did not control anything beyond that, and they didn't either. That is roughly that quarry between Zvornik. That was no man's land.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please put today's date there and KDZ-555.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is this a problem, the fact that it goes beyond -- actually, can it be admitted this way?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1613, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now have 1D4041 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In all of these villages -- actually, maybe we're going to call up the map again. Oh, sorry. Beg your pardon. Can we keep the map for a moment. Just mark Godus for us, where that review was of that unit. Well, we can use this map, yes. It's a different map, yes. Right. Godus. Godus, that's where the review was. Did all of these Muslim villages have their own units?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I know, all of them had their units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could this be admitted separately, or should we call up the other one, the previous one, and could we ask for Godus to be marked on that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think that's more convenient. Shall we upload Exhibit D1613 again.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just Godus, please.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. This --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- will be saved like this. Can we save this? So you marked in red. Yes. Let us continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 1D4041.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a report of the armed forces of the district of Tuzla. It's the Muslim army, and the date is the 10th of July, 1992. Could we now please have page 3. Unfortunately, the translation is coming in late, so I ask for your understanding, but I'm going to read this out. I'd like to draw your attention to the second paragraph where it says, "Results of combat operations." So it's the beginning of the month of June, and it says here: "From the beginning of the war to this day, the armed forces of Okrug --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, sorry to interrupt, but we have a translation if that will help.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And in the meantime, I ask the witness to read the passage and then we can put the English on the ELMO, and you can put the question. What part is the witness supposed to read?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely what he was saying.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no. You don't need to read out aloud. Just read it for yourself and wait for the --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: -- question by Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Results of combat operations, where it says, "From the beginning of the war until ..." Do you agree that this says from the beginning of the war defensive and offensive operations were conducted and significant results achieved, and that more than 70 per cent of the territory of the district was liberated, whereas only two municipalities were fully occupied and these two were Bijeljina and Sekovici?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Now we have it. We are on the same page?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. Let us see the section where it says "The result of combat activities." [In English] Next one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page -- "Results of combat operations," yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, now we can read. And what is your question, Mr. Karadzic, to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, is it correct that -- or what they are stating here, that 70 per cent of the district was held by them and that only two municipalities were, as they put it, occupied, these two being Bijeljina and Sekovici, and that most -- the most parts of the territories of 14 municipalities were liberated? And these are listed further down: Lukavica, Ugljevik, Zvornik, and others.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now get the following page, please. Let me just check. The English page may actually remain the same -- or, rather, leave it as it is. Can you see the section where it says -- no, no. The English page is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Next page for the B/C/S. Yes. It's coming, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see the third paragraph where it says: "In the past period of the war, and that is the first half of July, strong Chetnik strongholds were liquidated, Dubnica and Kalesija, Potpec, Lendici, Avramovina, Cerik," and others. Are these the settlements that correspond with Kozluk on our side?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the major populated places. Some of them are bigger than Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So they are saying that Chetnik strongholds were liquidated, that they were taken, the population was killed and the villages burned; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. In the next paragraph and the following paragraph, it says that over 300 Chetniks were killed and huge loss were is inflicted on the enemy with regard to materiel. And the next paragraph reads: "Currently, offensive activities are underway or being prepared at the fronts facing Tuzla, Kalesija, Zvornik," and so on; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, was there a single day without combat activity along the separation line between the Serbian and Muslim settlements in the Zvornik municipality? Could we say that fighting was a daily occurrence?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that only on a couple of days when cease-fires were signed there was no fighting. Apart from that, there was fighting all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm making mistakes because I'm in a hurry. Let me just check. No, that will do. I don't want to deal with this document anymore.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, this will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I note the time. It's time to take a break. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just very briefly, Your Honour. 1D03998, document that Mr. Karadzic called up in the beginning that does not have a date, that comes from the Drina Corps collection. So I believe the provenance is very solid there. Where the document came from is clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Then you would not object to the admission of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Then we can admit it. We will give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1615, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We will have a break for 20 minutes, after which you will have an hour, Mr. Karadzic, to conclude your cross-examination. We will resume at 10 to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellencies. Could we please see 1D3940.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But in relation to the list of volunteers, which is part of Drina Corps collection, I forgot to mention that it should be marked for identification pending English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, please look at this report of the Public Security Station Zvornik dated 26 June 1992, that encompasses the period from the beginning of April until the 20th of June. In the first paragraph, it says that on 5 May, there were combat activities between the Serbian Army and the Muslim-Croat extremists. Dragomir Mitrovic was taken prisoner. Could we please see the following page. It says here that his eyes were gouged out, his face mutilated, and legs also broken; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Item 4 shows that Bozidar Milic was also taken prisoner, then mistreated and finally killed. And then there were allegations of combat activities in the village of Kamenica on which occasion three members of the SJB were taken prisoner, Slavko Eric and others. Take a look at that. And after the body was examined at the Zvornik medical centre, it was established that he was tortured and finally killed; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we please see the following pages in both languages. So it's 4 and 5. These items are about that. And in Serbian we see that his left and right shoulder blades were broken, eyes gouged out, and so on. Did you know about this maiming and torturing of prisoners before they were killed?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: As is common knowledge, this man, Eric, was assistant commander for traffic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It goes on to say that Nikola Ivanovic was taken prisoner, and his corpse was also examined. In other words, whoever was taken prisoner was returned as a corpse.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in the village of Lipje, Slavko Simic was taken prisoner. That's item 9. It was established that he was mistreated and tortured and eventually killed. Then there's mention of Dragomir Milosevic in item 10. His corpse was taken over. And item 11 at Panduri, Milovan Tojic [phoen] was taken prisoner. He was a member of the military police. His throat was slit. And this is common knowledge among the people of Zvornik; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And in spite of that, until that time a considerable number of Muslims lived and worked in Zvornik; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1616, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On the occasion of one of the visits of Ms. Plavsic, who was a member of the Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina, did she then say that the Muslim civilian population should be protected?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Court's indulgence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us now see what the military situation was like. Could we please see 1D3938. 1D3938. This is a document of the Muslim army, arm of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Municipal Staff of the Zvornik armed forces. It says: "Report on the situation, organisation, establishment, structure and combat readiness of the Zvornik armed forces units." And it's dated 5 November 1992. Is it correct, then, that the Muslim part of Zvornik municipality was armed and had their armed forces and units rather than being a civilian zone.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They were equipped, and they had military units.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have page 3. [No interpretation] [In English] "Successful resistance was based on preparation." [Interpretation] Here it says the basis of the successful resistance was -- were the preparations that started months before the war that were reflected in the activity of many activists, organised armament, and resolution to resist at any cost. What is particularly important is the arrival of Captain Hajrudin Mesic. Is that that captain Hajro?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who together with Hodzic Mehdin Senad and a smaller number of organisers of the resistance managed to create an awareness of necessity of armed resistance. Mr. Witness, does that mean that they had to try to persuade the Muslims to fight the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at the top of this page where it says: Staffs of units were in Vlasenica, Bratunac, Srebrenica, in the Kamenica-Cerska-Srebrenica triangle. Settlements in that area were held independently. The Mali Zvornik, Ljubovija and Zvornik-Drinjaca roads were controlled and also spectacular operation was carried out to free hostages in Lipje. The road between Mali Zvornik and Ljubovija, is that on the territory of Serbia, and did they keep it under their own fire control successfully, nevertheless?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at this page and try to find the paragraph where it says that they tried to bring groups in. Nazif, Himzo, and others headed these groups. They got into our territory and they successfully got 7.500 civilians out from mid-July to mid-August. So they got their own civilians out to Tuzla; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And later on they tried to portray that as our ethnic cleansing; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's what I said about the number of inhabitants they had and about the number of inhabitants that left. In April when they reached an agreement with us, they had 4.000 inhabitants, whereas afterwards 1.600.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we go back one page. In Serbian too. It refers to Zvornik, doesn't it, the first paragraph? Then the second paragraph that Defence preparations started considerably earlier. And in the fourth paragraph it says -- or, rather, they recognise that the defence of Kula Grad was carried out when the JNA were still the legal armed force in the general Tuzla area; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then it says that in that period Kula Grad was synonymous with the BH resistance to aggression. Kula Grad showed that resistance was possible even in encirclement, and so on and so forth; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You confirmed to us that the Serb side had not intended to take Kula Grad had it not been this constant firing at civilians in Zvornik from Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we move two pages ahead now. I'd like to ask you to look at the beginning where operations are listed, operations that were carried out by these Muslim armed forces in Zvornik. And there's a reference to Sapna and Gaj and then the fight for Zaseok. They call it Zaseok. We call it Zaselia [phoen]. Then Brdjane, Odzacine, and then Boskovici, and so on. And you see down there cutting off a road and incursions by combatants in our rear, Noriso Grupa [phoen], Sekovici. The liberation of Rastosnica. Who did they liberate it from? It was only the Serbs who lived there.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was a village populated by Serbs 100 per cent. Also Boskovici, Odzacine, all those places are 100 per cent Serb, their population is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These locations that are referred to in this paragraph, the first paragraph, are you familiar with them? Are most of them Serb settlements that they attacked?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with the exception of Sapna and Gaj all the rest are Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you have a look at what it says in the penultimate paragraph that the armed forces of Zvornik operated as part of the units of the district staff of Tuzla, and that it was the Presidency of the Municipal Assembly that finances the logistics, and so on and so forth. Can we have the next page now? No. Beg your pardon. Let's have a look at what it says here in English. What were the goals? We see that in English here. Enlarging the units, replenishing units with officers -- actually we need the next page in Serbian now. You see what it says here, forming and equipping a multipurpose police company then manoeuvre units, and so on. And now can we have the next page in English too. You see where there are units, and you see how many interventions these units had, Godus, and that is a company, and then by this date they had 23 interventions?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that this refers to intervention platoons, and then you see that there is a total at the end. I think that that involves their number of personnel, actually.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Ah-ha. Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, I take it no objection from you. That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1617, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we briefly have a look at 1D4026. We are going to place the translation on the ELMO, with your leave, and we're going to see that the Serb side is beseeching the Muslim side to have an exchange carried out, and the Muslim side is returning mutilated corpses. Can we please have this enlarged a bit. Could the usher please place the translation on the ELMO. This is the 5th of May, 1992. These are requests, pleas, for exchanges. Can you have a look at this. There is a reference to Zaseok, Sestici, imprisoned persons.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here that the previous precondition had been met. The Muslims had made this a precondition. Our people actually did accommodate them, and is this not a plea? Is this not a cry for treating captured persons in a humane way?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1618, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 1D3997. Could we now have that, please. Unfortunately, the translation has not arrived yet, but are these your local communes? It says, "Local commune of Donje Kamenica, Gornja Kamenica, Lipje, Novo Selo and Snagovo." Are these local communities Muslim villages within the municipality of Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: As for these four local communes -- five local communes, are they asking Tuzla, the War Presidency of the municipality of Zvornik, to enhance the combat capacity? Can you actually have a look at this entire text?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They are asking for an increase in combat readiness, and they're asking for more resources, equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the next page now, because there is actually an explanation of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry. No objection, just what are we looking at actually? I may have missed it in the transcript, but where is this document -- what type of document is this? Where is it from?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you go back to the first page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, I'd like to read this out. These local communes are writing, and the subject is the situation in the free territory --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You're not giving evidence. I think Mr. Witness can tell us what this document is about in a brief way.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is information about the situation in the free territory of the mentioned local communes. These are local communities from Donja Kamenica, Gornja Kamenica, Lipje Novo Selo and Snagovo. They are from the municipality of Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you go to the last page, page 3. And who wrote this information?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What is written here is just the local communes of the mentioned areas. However, this does not show exactly who wrote this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was this not written up in Tuzla on the 12th of September, 1992?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have page 2. The one in the middle. I would like to draw your attention to subparagraph 2. Can you tell us what they say about the population here?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They say that during the first month they had about 15.000 people there, and that today that only half is left together with the members of the armed forces. They don't have a single doctor, and because of inadequate medical care civilians are dying on a large scale, pregnant women as they're trying to deliver their babies, soldiers who have been lightly wounded, et cetera. And also, when attempting to save lives when they were wounded, combatants often have the situation to try to help others in a makeshift way even by removing certain parts of their bodies, in parentheses, limbs.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not hear the question at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Restart asking your question. They did not hear that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: They say here that they had 15.000 people here and that only a half were left. Is that half -- that half that the previous document refers to when they say that they successfully managed to get them out? Did they get them out or did we expel them?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They mostly tried to get women, children, and men who were not of military age to Tuzla, whereas military-age men stayed on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be marked for identification?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: MFI D1619, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: 1D3941. I believe that there is a translation. Is this a dispatch of the MUP of Bijeljina where information is provided? That is the encircled part here, where information is provided about the Zvornik front line, and it says that it's peaceful, and Muslims from Vitnica and Zaseok, they fired at the Serbian villages of Petkovci and Sestici. The Muslim forces are trying to smuggle saboteurs into the free territory with the aim of spreading anxiety and killing civilians. These are specially trained saboteurs, trained in Sibenik and elsewhere in the Republic of Croatia. They call themselves the Mosque Doves. Did you know about that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this be admitted? I believe there's another page in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, all you did in relation -- in relation to this document is to read out some parts and then witness confirmed that it is written there as you read out. What's the point of putting these documents to the -- to the witness? You could have asked those questions without having to rely on this document. Can I hear from you on this point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would kindly ask Mr. Robinson to explain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Robinson.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think the question that he asked the witness was, "Did you know about that?" So the witness is confirming the events, not simply reconfirming that the text is appearing in the document. It's the same thing as asking the witness to confirm, "Is this consistent with your knowledge of those events." And I think the purpose of doing this is to corroborate the witness's testimony so that at the end of the day you're not being asked to simply take the witness's word for these events but we have corroborating documentation for it and that we think that would be an important element when the Chamber considers the credibility of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Chamber finds the explanation by Mr. Robinson understandable. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1620, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
