utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have 1D3942. While we are waiting, Mr. Witness, you mentioned in the examination of chief the name of Semsudin Muminovic, who unwillingly was the last to desert from the JNA, but he did desert eventually in early April; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at the order written by Mr. Semsudin Muminovic on the 16th of December, 1992. Instead of my reading it, can you please look at what kind of reorganisation in the Zvornik area is being ordered to be implemented by him. Can you look in all these villages such as Vitnica, Sapna, et cetera? Are you familiar with all of this, and is this a respectable military force that is being surrounded by unit -- units? Is this area surrounded by so many units?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Kovacevici, Kiseljak, Padjine, Sepak, Karakaj, Sapna, all of this is being reckoned by him to be his territory, and he has units in each of those places.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He kept the whole territory between Teocak all the way to Tuzla and Kalesija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Under item 2, he says the battalion shall be responsible for the following part of free territory: Zaseok to the left and Jefta.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So I'm not going to read all of these places, but anyway, he has troops deployed in all of them. Do you agree that this entire area, i.e., the Muslim part of Zvornik, was completely militarised?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that supports the map in which I made my markings and that is consistent with what he is saying here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have the next page in both versions, please. We have here Sutafar Tihir [phoen] company and Mosque Pigeons company, then some axes are being mentioned to be reconnoitered by Mosque Pigeons, Rozanj and Spasojevici, Djulici, Boskovici, Djakici [phoen], Klisa, et cetera. Does this indicate that the entire Muslim territory of Zvornik municipality was covered by military units that had very precise tasks?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We see that this was signed by Semsudin Muminovic, although the translators were unable to read it; is that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is the signature of Semsudin Muminovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1621, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have 65 ter 00621.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that you stated earlier and is it true that the Serbian authorities in Zvornik municipality called upon both the Muslims and the Serbs to go back to work and to come to live again in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we get a time-frame?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that immediately from the very beginning, i.e., in mid-April, the Serbian authorities called upon the people to go back to work, both the Muslims and the Serbs, and to come back to live in their own houses?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that was in early April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In other words, you're trying to say that while the authorities were operational, that's what they did?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After that, it made no sense, because the Muslims and the Serbs separated and they each had their pure -- ethnically pure territories.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please now focus on what -- on the 8th of May. The authorities of the Muslim municipality of Zvornik announced as a declaration for the population against the return. In order for me not to read everything, can you just say that what they say here is that they should take to arms to go to the forest. They are not to be placed -- not to place themselves at the disposal of the Territorial Defence, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is the essence of their declaration. Instead of going to the places under the Serb control, they are invited to go to the forest and put up resistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this also consistent with the fact that it was necessary to persuade the Muslims to fight?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Has the 65 ter number of this document been notified? What's the 65 ter number of this?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 621. That's how I called it, as 621.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No. That has been not reflected in the transcript, so that's why I asked the question. Yes. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1622, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Quite briefly, can we -- one -- at 1D1596. It's been admitted and MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Since this has been admitted, I won't spend too much time on this. Can you see that on the 10th of July it's being ordered to link up the Muslim territory in Podrinje through armed combat? Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And also mentioned, there are Kamenica and other parts of other municipalities. Does this include Zvornik, Bratunac, Srebrenica, and Vlasenica municipalities?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we briefly look briefly at 65 ter 16061.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: At this moment, we can fully admit the previous document without having to mark it for identification since we have the full translation. That will be done.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It bears the same number; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at this document. Is it true that in paragraph II it is said that here we have the commissioner's office -- or, rather, the commissioner Dragan Djokanovic. He says that due to the specific situation, the shortage of personnel, they failed to resolve the issue of the chief of the public security station and are therefore seeking help.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: For security reasons, armed civilians and soldiers should be prohibited in the town, except for police, military police, and persons with special authorisation; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That was in the beginning of July, and the [indiscernible] took place in late 1992. Dragan Djokanovic was making an inference here about the people who were subsequently arrested; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1623, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at 65 ter 16062 briefly. It shouldn't be broadcast, please. Please look at this document. This is the session of the Serbian Assembly of Zvornik. (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: (redacted) Can we now have page 4 in the Serbian, and I believe it's the same page in the English as well. It starts with item 9. Does it say here that the Assembly adopted the proposal and gave its support to the decision of the Serbian people to have the rule of law and to -- on the establish of war offices and disbanding of Crisis Staff, and that the Assembly insists on order to be resumed and to rectify all the irregularities, to evict all the people who were --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please tell where he's reading from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Interpreters cannot follow you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's because I'm in a hurry. I quite understand. Can we have the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this session, and do you remember that these conclusions were adopted, and do you remember that a huge number of enactments were adopted in order to introduce the rule of law?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Just a second. Shall we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We'll admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1624, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now look at 65 ter 18397. There's a translation of this document available. Please focus on this document, which is actually a report on the work of the public security station relating to July, August, and September. As a citizen and as the person who participated in the work of the Assembly, you were able to be informed about the situation. Now, look at paragraph 2. What kind of problems was this station facing, because it seems that paramilitary formations were the main problem.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us go to the following page in English. It's also the second paragraph in English. The difficulties are stated that made impossible the work of the station but also that of other state bodies. The activities of the paramilitaries contributed to a creation of an atmosphere of fear and uncertainty with the citizens and made possible theft and so on. Do you agree that these paramilitary groups took over policing without authorisation, set up check appointments where they took away cars and other goods from citizens without any authorisation to do so?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it goes on to say that the MUP special unit in late July routed the paramilitaries and enabled the station to assume its legal function again; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the examination-in-chief, Mr. Nicholls very skilfully tried to create the impression, or, perhaps that's how I understand it, that the arrest of these paramilitaries only came about because they maltreated the minister. Is it correct that these groups were arrested because of what we can read in this document or because they arrested the minister?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They engaged in lots of activities and the minister was only one. It was mostly because of the situation in Zvornik and because they harassed the Crisis Staff, the transitional government, because they took away people for executions and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct, and I would like to refrain from using the name of the late minister, they made him to eat grass and he wouldn't, and he almost got killed because of that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's common knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it says here that only on the 18th of September, with the assistance of military organs, the collection centre at Divic where there were 90 persons, mostly women, elderly persons, and children was disbanded; whereas in prison, there were 56 more persons. In Divic, we can conclude that there were mostly women, elderly persons and children. And is that what Grujic meant when he said that children were accommodated in abandoned facilities?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. Just I don't think he can say what another -- what Mr. Grujic meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree, Mr. Nicholls. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the following page in Serbian. I believe it's also found -- page in English. And there it says that a special difficulty in the work of the station was the impossibility to communicate with the Sarajevo CSBs by telephone which negatively affected the efficient tackling of some issues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that in line with what you know? It's the third paragraph.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we see the following page. I hope that you have understanding with regard to the English page. Does it say here that the police station in its daily work encounters many problems among which there are insufficient personnel strength, insufficient training level, and the shortage of pistols, only 20 per cent have pistols, the shortage of cuffs. There were no off-road vehicles. The existing rolling stock that is nine vehicles have gasoline engines. And at that time policing is done by paramilitaries who have no authorisation to do that. And they have made stockpiles of Golf vehicles in their yards; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see the following page. In English, it's section B. We see that 102 criminal offences reported, of which 55 were solved. And there's a break-up of these offences, and then they go on to say that because the court and the municipal prosecutor's office are not functional --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: We didn't hear the end of the question -- or, rather, the question that the accused put.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The last part of the question was not recorded right. We should go to the following page in English. It says that because the court and the district prosecutor's office are not functional, 31 criminal reports were not submitted. What is meant is probably 31 more reports; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: To your mind, these 52 per cent or so of solved crimes under the circumstances is a considerable success?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1625, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I get a discount, as it were, to show some more documents and a video that will -- that will contribute to a better understanding of the relations on the part of the Trial Chamber? Is it my turn?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I didn't follow what you meant by "discount."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked for some additional time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think you have around five minutes to conclude. And can I ask you for planning purpose how much time would you need for your redirect, Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We have less than half an hour, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Conclude before -- by 12.00, when we can have a break. You have 10 minutes, 10 or 12 minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we take a look at 65 ter -- or was this one admitted? Does it have a new number? Let's then look at 65 ter 12158.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that this is an official note of the Crime Prevention Administration at Pale, that is the MUP headquarters? And here on page 1, 18 names of arrested persons are listed. These are mostly persons born in Zvornik, but there are also two Hungarians from Vrsac, number 13 and 14; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the -- the others are all born in Zvornik, more or less.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see the following page -- or, rather, page 3 since it contains the authentication. [In English] Is it admitted already, no?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: My question was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry. Just my question was is this on the list? I can't seem to find it in what we got.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] On the list -- well, possibly we omitted to put it on the list in time, but I kindly ask for understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see the following names in the signature block, Ljubomir Kovac, Sasa Blagojevic, and Dejan Vaskovic? And do we see 21 names, and among them Pivarski. Stojan Pivarski is number 17 on page 1. And let me ask you, on the seventh line from the bottom, some of them who used to be under the command of Vojin Vuckovic joined this unit several days prior to being arrested and had not participated in the current activities of combat operations. Is that the reason why they were not detained but instead sent to regular units?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document, after which I would like to show some very short video-clips that will illustrate the relationship between Kula Grad and Zvornik, and so on. Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: These are interviews --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is an official report about the arrest of 21 persons. It's the MUP headquarters submitting the report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Not interviews themselves. Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. This will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D1626, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellencies. I called up this document most of all to show why not everybody was arrested. This document shows that there wasn't a reason for some persons --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Objection, argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is not the time for your statement or submission. You have five minutes to --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let us take a look at 1D389. This should be a video-clip. It should be the view of Zvornik from Kula Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was Zvornik named after the -- a church or belfry from olden times, and was there a very old Christian church from the 12th or 13th century?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That is how the town was named. The church was built at the time of Djuradj Brankovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the view of Zvornik from Kula Grad, and were civilians shot at from this location?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection, but just for the record is this created -- a recent video; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: With that understanding, we will admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1627, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get 1D3990. It's also a view of both Zvornik and Mali Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And let me explain that Mali Zvornik is a part of town that is in Serbia and it is now and has always been a separate municipality.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this Mali Zvornik, as seen from Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1628, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see 1D3992. We'll skip one because there isn't time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is Kula Grad, the fort; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can Divic be seen from here? And the peninsula, is that Divic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it can clearly be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And this is the dam, and Divic is in the upper part; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And Divic has a mosque, as we can see here, and that was a Muslim settlement?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, predominantly Muslim.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So from Kula, they were able to shoot at any house and any street; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: With the same understanding, we'll admit this as Exhibit D1629.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we see one last thing, 1D3995.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is Kula Grad as seen from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Exhibit D1630. Your last question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever know of any bad intentions or wicked plan on the part of the regular authorities with regard to any individual group in your municipality?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your evidence and for your patience. I was in a hurry, and it may not all have been very clear, but thank you for understanding.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're welcome.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls, I told you that we would have a break before your redirect, but if you could conclude, as you indicated, in less than half an hour, we can continue before the break and start with the next witness in the next session. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, sir, you were asked a lot of questions today about military formations of the Muslim units, Muslim paramilitaries, when they took certain towns, where they were -- where they were based, how they were armed. Do you remember answering all those questions?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did answer those questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And at the period we're talking about, at no time were you a member of -- or you tell me, were you a member with the TO or the VRS up to the end of 1992?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was mobilised for about two or three months, not more than that. I held these positions in the business community.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yeah. So while you had the position you told us about, you were also mobilised. For which months?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm for the sure. I think it was sometime in May, and then as we were directors from various firms, the army would mobilise us during holidays when people did not work for a few days, and then we went to help out the regular army, just to give them a break of a few days. But on the whole in 1992, it wasn't more than 60 to 80 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I have 65 ter 22022, please. It's a map. All right, sir. This is a map entitled -- military map, obviously, entitled "Operation Priboj." We can see it's from January 1993, from the command of the Drina Corps. It's hard to read in this size, but it's in the translation at the top left.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can blow up the map a little bit so that we can see clearer the area within the blue lines. All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, now, from your military experience, and it's basic knowledge for those of us who work in this Tribunal, the red lines are -- is the outline of the Serb side's positions, trenches; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And then the area inside would indicate the area held at this point by the ABiH or Muslim forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. Using that electronic pen which you've seen -- you've used before, could you please mark where Konjevic Polje is on this map.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we put a 1 by that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And could you please mark Udrc -- or, sorry, I have trouble pronouncing this, Udrc to the left. I can spell it: U-r-d-ch [sic].

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't see it. It's somewhere between Drinjaca and Konjevic Polje here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Which bears the number 1042?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I didn't hear your words through interpretation, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Does Mr. Nicholls mean 1402 on the left-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, sir, I don't think you'll mind me leading here. If you look to the west and north and look up, you'll see that mountainous region with 1042 on it.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Mark that with a 2, please.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And just a couple more. Paljevine.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I lived on the other end of the municipality, so I have heard of all of these villages, but I'm not sure whether I can actually find my way.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, this one, I think, we can skip that. We can skip that. Kamenica and Snagovo. You know where those are, I'm sure.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We may need to pull the map down a bit, please, so that he can see higher on the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's difficult. After having made these markings, we can -- or we can zoom out and then do the exercise again.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, you know, to save time, I'll keep moving, Your Honours. If we can just mark this, I think we all know where Kamenica is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We -- we have a mark in Kamenica. Shall we put number 3 for that?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And if we can save this and then we can just move out and see where Snagovo is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could you put the date and your signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: KDZ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your number.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we delete that, and you need to sign as your number, which is KDZ-555.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And I omitted one other point just before we have the witness -- before we save it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And, sir, before --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: 555, yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And before we save that, could you also please mark Cerska.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never been there, but I can see it's there on the map. I've never heard of it until the UN resolution was passed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And number 4.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. So you grew up in this region, spent time there as an adult, worked in the occupation we've heard about, and you never heard of Cerska? Just making sure that's --

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. Believe me. Half of the people of Zvornik -- believe me, before the UN resolution on Cerska was passed, I had never heard of it, and I hadn't known that it was in the area of the municipality of Zvornik. If you were to ask half of the people from Zvornik whether they had heard of Cerska before that, they hadn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: We can save that please. And we've seen now the area, the front lines in the beginning of 1993, the very beginning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll give the next Prosecution exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That will be Exhibit Number P3160.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So what was the question in relation to these places?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Well, just, Witness, we can see -- you agree with me that these areas you've marked are either inside the Muslim-controlled region or just on the edge?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends on the period we're talking about. If we're talking about the end of 1992, they were under the control of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm talking about January 1993.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: January 1993? Under the control of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, could I bring up P2085, please. All right, Witness, you know who Miljenka Ivanovic is; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was commander of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right let's look at this order of his from 24th November 1992, a couple of days of Mr. Karadzic visited Zvornik. Because of time, I want to just look at this very urgent decision for further operations. Under paragraph 1, if you look in your language you'll see what the order is -- what the decision is: "Launch an attack using the main body of troops and major equipment to inflict on the enemy the highest possible losses, exhaust them, break them up and force them to surrender, and force the Muslim local population to abandoned the area of Cerska, Zepa, Srebrenica and Gorazde." And then it continues. Did you read that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we go to the next page. And go down to the portion -- to point 3(c) so that can be read.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Serbian version I don't have it. There's only 3(a).

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]... yeah, here we have it. This is: "Moral and psychological preparations: Before initiating any kind of operation, inform the unit members about the important aim of that operation and underline that the outcome of minor actions and of the whole operation is of a crucial importance for the realisation of the aim of the Serbian people, namely, the creation and establishment of a Serbian state in these areas." So, Witness, you testified -- Witness, you testified today on cross-examination about your understandings of the object of the Serbian people and any questions from Mr. Karadzic and about Muslim operations. Let me ask you, this operation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Is English channel working okay? It's now working, but -- I think the witness has been following you, as well as the transcript. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So you were aware of this operation to remove the Muslim population -- Muslim population from the area we saw on that map, some of the places?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we as citizens understood that the aim was to link up the territory. They were holding some territory and split our forces into two parts, and we didn't have -- we couldn't communicate with half of the Republika Srpska. The objective was to open the road through Konjevic Polje and it was also economically significant because ore could be brought to Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I now have 65 ter 21955.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sir, you're familiar with the officer named Svetozar Andric?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Just very quickly, following up on the map we saw and the order from General Zivanovic, I'd like you to look under paragraph 3 here, which -- we need to go to the next page in the Serbian. Thank you. And here we see Andric reporting to the Drina Corps command, to Zivanovic. Shortly after that order we saw: "In the course of the day, special units of the 1st Birac Light Infantry Brigade took and destroyed the village of Gobelji thus fleeing -- freeing up the left flank of the main forces in the attack on Cerska." And if I could look at now, and then the last question, 08265. The 2nd of March, another report to the Drina Corps command by Andric. If you look at paragraph 2: "Our forces which are moving in the wider area of Kamenica, Gajici and Grobici worked according to the plan without major problems. The village of Gobelji has been burnt and tomorrow the plan is to do Paljevine." Signed again, Andric.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It says Paljevine, but I believe it's the village of Paljevici so it doesn't signify that anything was burned.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, to burn Paljevine, which is a region; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: He said the plan for tomorrow is to do Paljevine, but I believe that it's the village of Paljevici, and it says that the village of Gobelji has been burnt.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes. And it says the plan tomorrow is to do Paljevine. Now my question is: You showed a lot of knowledge answering yes to these very long questions by Mr. Karadzic about containing many, many facts of Muslim military operations. Is this correct that same knowledge you had at the time, that these operations were undertaken, these villages were burnt in order to create a Serbian state in this region?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have an objection. Can I state it? The question implies something that was not said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. It has the nature of a leading question. Could you reformulate it, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Witness, what do these, from your knowledge, and I've shown you these documents -- what was the aim of these military operations we have just looked at? And how did they tie into the plan of the Serb people, desires of the Serb people at that time?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, and we're talking about 1993, I had an official position in the municipality of Zvornik. I was aware of this operation, and I understood it this way: That its objective was to reach a line at Divici, which is 2 kilometres from Zvornik, and thus put an end to constant attacks. The second goal was to liberate the road that connects the eastern part of Republika Srpska with the rest, and it has a great economic significance because the largest factory had its supply road from Milici that way. And --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat what he said about Konjevic Polje.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you repeat what you said about Konjevic Polje. The interpreters couldn't hear that part.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Without that road through Konjevic Polje, the Republika Srpska was divided into two parts.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Could I have 02955, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Did you mind to tender those two documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]... Mr. Andric. We'll admit them each.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibits P3161 and 3162 respectively.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: This is not 02955, unless I have my -- unless my number is correct. Exhibit number, sorry, 02955. I should have said P.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Now, a little bit earlier, December 1992, Witness, I'd like you to look at the third paragraph here. This ties into what we were talking about, as well as your testimony today about paramilitaries, and I'll read it out. This is another Drina Corps document: "With the arrival of paramilitary organisations to the Zvornik municipality, particularly the arrival of Arkan and his people, this territory was liberated from the Turks. Turks made up 60 per cent of the municipality's population and now it has been cleansed and replaced with an ethnically pure Serb population." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: And this is signed by the chief of the organ for operations and training, Miladin Prstojevic. Did you know him?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can you reconcile that assessment with some of what -- the yes answers we've been hearing from you today? If you could explain it.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, these are both correct. Most of the municipality of Zvornik in late 1992 was controlled by Muslim units, which can be seen from the map that you also showed, and it's also true that this report written on the 17th of December, 1992, that the part controlled by the Serbs was ethnically pure. There was an insignificant number of Muslims and Croats who left behind, maybe a hundred or not more. Everything else was ethnically -- ethnically pure. I mean, if that's the gist. Because the passage under that says that a large number of Serbs was brought in and settled here and that corroborates this story.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So if I understand, you agree that this assessment is accurate.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection. The witness did not agree.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said that he writes here -- or can you analyse it if you want. The Zvornik municipality was liberated by the Turks, which means that it's ethnically clean, and it's much less than one-half of the municipality where the Serbs lived. And in December 1992, it was almost -- almost ethnically pure because a negligible number of Muslims and Croats lived there. And it goes on to say that their [indiscernible] Arkan and his people, this territory was liberated from the Turks. The Turks made up 60 per cent of the municipality's population. It has been cleansed and replaced with an ethnically pure Serb population. Well, this is not correct. No Serb soldiers went beyond Sapna. Major Jago Dus [phoen] and so on. Then there's Zaseok, Nezuk, and the other villages, Zuje Carci [phoen] and many more. There were no combat activities there ever because the Muslims were always the majority there and they controlled that all the time. Even now they belong to the federation of BH according to the ethnic division.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sorry, I would need about five more, minutes if I may, for one small discrete --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I have to inquire of the technical booth whether we have tape for the five minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we can go for five minutes more.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Very quickly, sir, and be as quick as you can, do you know where the village of -- or small hamlet of Scemlija is, just a little bit to the west of Zvornik, close by Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Scemlija.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. How far is that from Zvornik? What is the distance from Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Scemlija is not even two kilometres away from Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: All right. Could I have D1610, please. This is the intercept. And if I could go to the last two pages, please. We've already seen this. Second to last page of the English. All right. Now, you've testified that there was no person such as Milorad Bogicevic in Zvornik, to your knowledge; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Let's look quickly because we didn't go through it in much detail when Mr. Karadzic brought it what is said about the weapons. On page 4 of the English: "Karadzic: Hubre [phoen] handed out weapons. "Bogicevic: He fuck it. "Karadzic: That's not true. Don't fuck with me. Why do you but bullshit over the phones? It's not true that anybody from the party has something to do with the distribution of weapons. Are you mad? "Bogicevic: Fuck it. "Karadzic: Fuck what? One of you fuck it a little. "Bogicevic: Here at our place." On the next page in English. "Karadzic: Where at your place? Don't give me this bullshit over the phone. Bye. "Bogicevic: Have a nice day." Again this was from suggest 1991. Again, you've never heard of this man, Bogicevic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The family name of Bogicevic is present in the Zvornik municipality. I believe they live around the Drinjaca, but I've never heard of Milorad Bogicevic, nor was there such a person in any structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So you haven't hear of him. P2872, please. This is a payroll of TO members of the Serbian municipality of Zvornik for the month of May, 1992. Could we go to the next page in B/C/S and the next page in English. That's the correct page of the English. Could we keep going through the B/C/S, to the last page of the B/C/S. Excuse me. All right. This is a 10th of June, 1992, receipt to confirm that Stojan Pivarski has received money for the special purpose unit. Now very quickly, Stojan Pivarski was a volunteer or paramilitary leader; correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Okay. What's the first name on the list of men for the May payroll for the Pivarski special unit? Read it out.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Milorad Bogicevic from Scemlija.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: So now do you still think that that phone call was from an anonymous person?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if this man, Milorad Bogicevic, existed. Because, you know, a man in Zvornik whom I don't know, and you can check whether anybody else knows it, it's unlikely that he would call up the president or the political party. I mean, I don't know. But I still claim I don't know Milorad Bogicevic, and I doubt that there is such a person in Scemlija because there is nobody with that last name at Scemlija (redacted) (redacted) People from Vercevici [phoen], Baljkovica, Zevalje [phoen], Setici, and so on, are mentioned here. So I'm not sure if this might not be a Milorad Bogicevic who is a volunteer, because this is in the context of Pivarski.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours, very much, for the extra time.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have just a minute or half a minute?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In relation to this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, in relation to Cerska and that area. I only need half a minute, not more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, just one question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to make it easier for you, Cerska belongs to Vlasenica. That's why I didn't know it. Please, can you confirm that the concentration of Kamenica and Rudic, and so on, were places that we left alone for a year. When we asked them not to fight us, whereas they did fight us every day, and there was a military justification. And -- and they fought in civilian clothes. Can you confirm that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Slavkovic was killed when he went to Kamenica to negotiate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mean the negotiator [Realtime transcript read in error, negotiate"] was killed?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-555 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Witness. That concludes your evidence at the Tribunal. On behalf of the Tribunal and the Bench, I would like to thank you for your coming to The Hague to give it. So now you're free to go, but please wait until the curtain is prepared.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: "Negotiator." I would like to intervene in the transcript. "The negotiator was killed."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break for half an hour and resume at 10 past 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. As you know, we'll have to move into private session for the next witness. I wanted to do that quickly now, because I have two unrelated matters that need to be raised in private session as well, and I thought it best to do that before the witness entered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We go back -- go to private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. We are in open session. It's about the witness after next, KDZ-029. I noted that a file has been -- a motion has been filed, and I follow that you understand what it is about.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder whether Prosecution can orally respond to that motion tomorrow morning at the beginning of tomorrow morning's hearing, and I -- I hope that in the response the Prosecution should identify why that one page proofing note referred to in the motion was not disclosed earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think we're in the process of expediting a written response as well. I understand the Court's interest is in getting a response as quickly as possible for very understandable reasons. I take it that if we are able to complete the written submission in the same period of time the Court would also welcome that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's bring in the witness. We go to private session -- or we don't have to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. If you could take the solemn declaration, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Please make yourself comfortable. Please be seated. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, I didn't know if the Court wished to -- I note it has in the past occasionally described the nature of the protective measures. I don't insist the Court do so, I just didn't know if that was something the Court intentionally omitted or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, I take it you received explanation as to the nature of the protective measures which has been allowed to you, but you will be addressed as a specific number, which is KDZ-340, without naming your real name, and whenever we -- why don't we show him the image which is being broadcast. And you will not be seen by anybody other than those in the courtroom, and your image will show like this. So you will not be identified by anyone outside the courtroom. So whenever we deal with some confidential information which may reveal the identity of yourself, we will go into private session, which means nobody can follow what we are discussing inside the courtroom. And the transcript as well of those parts will not be disclosed to anybody other than the parties of this case. Do you follow? Do you understand that, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please bear in mind we have to rise exactly before quarter to 2.00. Yesterday the other hearing has to be delayed by five minutes because of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Understood, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: Thank you. Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Witness, I'd first like to call up a document that is designated as 65 ter 90259. This won't be broadcast. We are in private session. And I'd like you to confirm by simply indicating yes or no whether or not this accurately indicates your name and date of birth -- or your name. Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And I'd tender that, Your Honour, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3164 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We go to private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Two additional matters quickly, Mr. Witness: At page 7 of your amalgamated statement, you state that Aco Sekanic was part of the TO staff, and you think he was the assistant commander or something like that but you're not a hundred per cent sure. Do you know whether or not -- well, I understood you wanted to clarify that in connection with whether or not you knew that Mr. Sekanic was an assistant commander.

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: Aco Sekanic, since there were several assistant commanders in the staff for logistics for operations and so on and so forth, he was a type of assistant commander of his. Now, which function he had in the staff, I really cannot say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And finally at page 5 of your statement, you refer to a Mr. Sejfudin Hadziefendic and I understood that you wanted to correct that name to Hadziavdic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: That is right. His real name is Sejfudin Hadziavdic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Mr. Witness, with those clarifications can you confirm that the testimony and statements in the Krajisnik and Stanisic cases which have been incorporated into the amalgamated statement accurately reflect your information and statement at the time, and if asked about the same issues again, you would provide the same information and that that information is truthful?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: Yes, I'd give the same answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I'd tender 90258, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be admitted.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit P3165 under seal, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, I have not too many follow-up questions. I don't know if we can address them in the time remaining, but we'll do our best. First of all, at page 2 of your amalgamated statement, you referred to Zvornik city being taken over on the 9th of April. Can you tell us which forces took over Zvornik city on the 9th of April?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: Up until the 9th of April, Zvornik was under the control of the Muslim staff of the TO and their police. They controlled Zvornik from Metaris [phoen] to Karakaj, and over here in Zvornik towards Kula it was the Muslim forces that exercised control. After Zvornik was liberated from the Muslim forces on the 9th of April, it is the Serb forces that took control over of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, at page 5 of your statement as indicated a moment ago, you provided information about your contact with Mr. Hadziavdic, Sejfudin Hadziavdic. He was the Muslim man who had been taken to the Crisis Staff and about whom you said was a good man and should be released. So a couple of questions in connection with that. You said that you reported to the Crisis Staff at page 2 to 3 of your statement on the 13th of April. Was that the first occasion on which you reported to the Crisis Staff the occasion on which you saw Mr. Hadziavdic, or did that occur on another occasion?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: That happened on another occasion, because on the 9th of April, in the afternoon, I left Zvornik and I went to visit my family. On the 13th of April, I returned to Zvornik, and I reported to the Crisis Staff. On that occasion, I did not see Hadziavdic. However, afterwards, when I came to report to the Crisis Staff, on one occasion, I cannot remember the exact date or time, it was sometime in the evening. He was brought to the Crisis Staff with his son and the men who were there, I don't know who brought him, I asked -- they asked whether I knew him because he saw me from the car and he said he knew me. I know him. He was an exceptionally honest and honorable man. When the war was on in Croatia, he wanted to help there as well. He sent help via the Red Cross from Mali Zvornik. So if it is that way, take the man home, apologise to him, that's what they did, and I don't know what happened to him and his son after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And how often did you report to or appear at the Crisis Staff and for what reasons?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: I reported to the Crisis Staff sometimes once and sometimes twice a day. Sometimes once in two days, because there was duty service in the streets, because above Zvornik, up until the 27th of April, Kula Grad which dominates over Zvornik was controlled by Muslim forces, so it was necessary to patrol the area because it's about a kilometre or a kilometre and a half from Zvornik to Kula Grad. However, as the crow flies, it is only a few hundred metres or even less than that to the first houses in Zvornik and that is why we had this duty service.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you or others report to the Crisis Staff for such purposes as getting movement passes?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: Passes were given for free movement through the town itself and also in order to get to Serbia. That's the kind of passes that were issued by the Crisis Staff. Sometimes I reported for this and sometimes for that, but it depended on what was necessary. So when I was on duty in the street, I was even on duty with Muslims so that was no problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Let me ask a couple of questions about the patrol duty you referred to. First of all, was that in your own neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, in my neighbourhood, because that's where I know people, who they are, what they do. I know everyone. So we had that duty service there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And was primarily a Muslim or a Serb area?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: In that neighbourhood, there were a few Serb houses but there were also quite a few Muslim houses, so practically all the houses opposite my house were Muslim houses. There were only one or two houses in my immediate neighbourhood that were Serb houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Did you have weapons for patrol or while you were on patrol?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: During these patrols and walkabouts, we did not have any weapons. And once when some volunteers came by, and I didn't know them, they gave me and my Muslim neighbour a hand grenade each. They said, You shouldn't walk around just like that. You never know who you are going to come across. So on that occasion that neighbour of mine also got this hand grenade. When we finished our duty, then he gave me this hand grenade that he had. And he said, If they search for them I don't want to have one on me because if that were to happen, we don't know what would follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: This man that you referred to that you patrolled with was -- when you had earlier stressed what a good man Mr. Hadziavdic was, what can you say about this man you were patrolling with?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: Well, I cannot say that my neighbours were bad people, although before there were clashes in the town of Zvornik many of them went out into the streets with weapons, automatic weapons, long barrelled ones. They had these weapons they received from the police and I cannot say how, so they had long barrelled weapons and they went out into the streets. I don't know why, either because they were afraid of us or I don't know why, but otherwise I can say that they were rather honest people, most of them that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And this man in particular that you were patrolling with?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: Also an exceptionally honest boy because he's younger than I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Is he still in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: No. I think that he now lives in Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And did you learn what happened to him such that he left Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ-340
utterances.text: Well, because of this exchange that took place, because some soldiers had been arrested and taken to Kula, they brought him into custody. When he went to report it, the company that he worked in, in Glinica, they brought him in. They brought him to the police, and I heard that he was beaten up and so on and so forth. But for the sake of this exchange, to give Muslims for Serbs who had been captured. What happened after that I don't know, but I do know that both he and his family left Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Witness, at page -- I think we have to move into private session for this matter, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll rise for today and continue tomorrow morning at 9.00. Mr. Witness, you must have been told, but you are not supposed to discuss with anybody about your testimony you're giving. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I understand that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Tomorrow, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Friday, the 19th day of August, 2011, at 9.00 a.m.
